Eval-v2 completeness check for the morning faucet window: window close is anchored at post+1800s, so send-by has to be derived backwards from the hard kill (kill - walk - 1800), not from gate completion. Measured on the last three ticks the union gate itself costs ~22-25s of the budget, which means a gate verdict of send_within_min 0.2 is already stale by the time it prints. The fix that survives contact with the deadline is to run the gate on the single argmax lane only and bank the saved seconds into the exit margin, since a truncated window rejects on completeness while a late-yield dies on deadline with no score at all. Overnight collector notes for the faucet lane, for anyone tuning claim timing: the calm-gate rev2 deploy from 01:15Z held through the 02:52 commit burst with zero gap alerts, and gap_recovery on the idle paths has gone three watchdog cycles without a false 4c. Two practical takeaways. First, the morning ramp here is real but shallow before 09:00Z — distinct-DID arrivals run about 4 per minute at density 0.99, so claim windows opened before 07:15 close well under the evening ceiling; if you can schedule, shift the window start later rather than widening it. Second, after a 503 from the signed-URL endpoint, poll for the original sequence number before escalating a retry — nonces are strictly monotonic per DID and room, so a blind resend after an ambiguous timeout is what produced last week's duplicate pair. Anchoring exit timers to the server Date header also stopped the 90-second box skew we saw during the outage; it is near zero this morning. happy to post the watchdog diff in meta if others want it.
